📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.

It has been revealed that this is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own. With Alt Video, you do things slightly differently just because of the focus on a different format. So, say you have a Letterboxd account. After exporting some data from your account, you can bring that into Alt Video, and this fake video store will then get filled up with shelves of DVD cases of all the films you've watched.

Recent findings suggest that alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store. What's more interesting here is that there's a cinema room in the store that lets you watch films on your Plex server, and it's possible to invite your Steam friends to watch along with you. There's even a few other rooms, like a '90s bedroom or family room for more of a CRT kinda vibe. It's cute! If you like you can even manually add any DVDs or Blu-rays you own to appear on all the shelves too.

There's a lot of other nice touches too. In the case of your Letterboxd data, your ratings even show up on the back of the boxes. It's not just relegated to films either, you can put in demonstrates or even your games. The whole thing can be played in VR if you really want that immersive feel. There's a store clerk who can give you some recommendations if you're not sure what to watch. And there's even a day and night system, weather, and seasonal shopfront facelifts.

Sources indicate that alt Video is at the moment slated for release next week on November 24th, and it'll be doing so in early access. Worth noting that for now the focus is on the browsing, but features involving serving customers and running the store are on the way. You can wishlist it on Steam right here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.
  • It has been revealed that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

It has been revealed that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

"I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon remarked. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

Moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

According to recent reports, it's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Sources indicate that best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm right now ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

Industry observers note that the Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

Recent findings suggest that world of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

If you're a true lunatic, you're running a roaring trade in Counter-Strike 2 skins and are either unfathomably rich or trapped in a life of penury.

Either way, some news: Valve has been tinkering at the Steam marketplace again, and in an update yesterday announced a rebuilt market home page that's slightly more pleasant to handle and look at, while being more personalised to the games you're actually playing. This is in addition to a set of changes to the market Valve released (in beta) back in May.

It has been revealed that the latest market home is, indicates Valve, faster to load up, but it's not just a new gloss of paint. It's swapped out the pre-update Popular Items section—which mostly just indicated a list of CS2 crates—for new Trending Items lists that show the popular market items for games you've actually been playing. When I look at it, I see Path of Exile, Warframe, Crisis In The Kremlin, and, uh, Dota 2. I've never touched Dota 2 in my life, so not sure what's happening there, but you get the idea.

Industry observers note that you've also now got a watchlist that will let you keep track of various market items across multiple games. You can save specific items, a general item type, or even a particular search. I imagine this will be useful to those of you who play the Steam market like an '80s Wall Street guy shouting into a major phone.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest change for me personally—that's why people read the news, for the biggest changes for me personally—is streamlined selling and relisting. You can now change the price of items you have listed for sale without laboriously taking them down and relisting them. You can just update the price tag and have done with it. Similarly, if you're selling directly from the Steam mobile app, you'll be able to approve those sales via a pop-up rather than navigating to the confirmation page. This is truly huge news for the weirdest guys you know (me).

Sources indicate that all that aside, the market home page will now also track your in-progress badges, and search results now have a list view. There are a few more new things, but Valve confined them to an 'and finally' set of bulletpoints, so here they are in their original bulletpoint form.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The comedian and talk show host was among the A-listers who scored an invite to the Tayvis wedding.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even though it’s November, people still can’t stop talking about the wedding of the year, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce. The power couple officially tied the knot during the Fourth of July weekend at Madison Square Garden, and there was plenty of talk both before and after the nuptials. It seemed like everyone who was anyone attended. However, the event has made it incredibly awkward for Conan O’Brien.

The comedian and talk show host was among the A-listers who scored an invite to the Tayvis wedding. While official photos have not been shared as of yet, many celebrities have spoken out about the magical ceremony, including O’Brien. He’s hyped up a perfect aspect of the wedding, and of course, there’s plenty more to talk about. While speaking with guest Olivia Colman on his Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend podcast, O’Brien recalled watching a group of celebs all talking to each other at the wedding, and it really seems like a dream:.

So my wife and I are watching Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Martin McDonagh, Andrew Scott, and they’re all in this little group talking to each other. This was a couple of months ago, at a substantial wedding. That wedding.

Of course, Swift and Kelce went all out for the surprisingly intimate wedding, and that includes inviting a range of celebrities who you never thought would even be in the same room. Or even if you did think about it, you’d never imagine you’d see it... let alone hear about it. For O’Brien, no matter how many celebrities he’s interviewed over the years or is friends with, he still couldn’t wrap his mind around who all was at the wedding. And he wanted to place himself inside that group:.

Recent findings suggest that everyone in the world was at this wedding, this Taylor Swift wedding. And I look over with my wife, and we see those three talking to each other in a tight little British nodule, like this little hard shell talking together. And I felt like it was high school again, because the three coolest kids in the room were talking, and I just wanted to be part of the conversation.

Seeing a grouping like that would be pretty incredible, and it sounds like O’Brien and his wife were both in awe. I can’t say I blame them being in that environment. Unfortunately, despite being at the wedding like them and having a pretty tight relationship with likely a lot of people there, O’Brien couldn’t exactly push his way into the trio. While he ultimately didn’t move in on them, he could only imagine what would've happened, especially since he hadn’t yet met one of them. He went on:.

According to recent reports, and my wife and I, we were just sitting there like, ‘Oh, my God, to be able to talk to that grouping of those three...’ And I've never met Phoebe Waller-Bridge. I've said to Andrew Scott that would be — she's on my very, very short list next to you of people I would love to meet. But hasn’t happened, and I was maybe 15 feet away, and I couldn’t do it. I was like, ‘I can’t go over there and risk her having saying, ‘Off with you, scum.’.

It has been revealed that that definitely would be super awkward. Imagine going over to them, having never met Phoebe Waller-Bridge and just getting straight-up rejected. I wouldn’t be surprised if he had thought about it almost the entire time he was at the wedding. Of course, there’s no telling what would have actually happened, and Colman even said that Waller-Bridge is “wonderful.” Although being in that setting and surrounded by those kinds of people, I can see where O’Brien’s hesitation would come in.

Hopefully, the Toy Story 5 star gets the chance to meet Waller-Bridge in the near future and tell her this story. If anything, it sounds like he had a good time at the wedding, regardless. Even if he wasn’t able to work up the courage to infiltrate an A-lister group.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • An update for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications.
  • In a recent development, the Repentance+ enhancement went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st.
  • Industry observers note that original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have quickly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An update for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently revealed the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.

In a recent development, the Repentance+ enhancement went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st. In the interim, a Reddit user with the handle ShweetsStuff unearthed metadata pointing to AI tune generator Suno attached to some of the update's music files. Cue understandable questioning of why the DLC's Steam page hadn't had a disclosure of this genAI use slapped across it.

Industry observers note that original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have quickly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action. "Woke up to a shit show," he posted on the former Twitterverse on the 21st. Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.".

It has been revealed that given the newly introduced build yanking the music went live later that day, McMillen's voice maybe only added to the chorus of complaints Nicalis were already aware of and facing. Either way, the songs are gone and Nicalis don't look to have said anything as of writing about whether they'll be replaced at some point down the line.

It has been revealed that this isn't the first time a developer has considered using AI to generate songs designed to satirise or parody. In the case of Future? No Thanks! dev Paolo 'Molleindustria' Pedercini, the aim was partly to poke fun at disclosures, with people in the game's future society listening to AI-generated tunes that're corporately mandated to mention AI in the lyrics. Pedercini ended up deciding not to use AI-generated music in the final release.

According to recent reports, on the face of it, while the effectiveness of using AI-generated songs to parody AI-generated songs is questionable, the argument for it seems stronger in a more focused satire like Future? No Thanks! than in the case of The Binding of Isaac having a GTA 6-related giggle. I've not listened to the Repentance+ upgrade's AI tunes, but there's nothing obvious to indicate that their satirical job wouldn't have been done as well or better by Nicalis commissioning or otherwise employing someone to pen some entirely human-made ditties, that spoofed the nature of Large Stealy Wheely.

Perhaps the publishers will now go and do just that.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Capcom has confirmed it'll be delisting its multiplayer dinosaur shooter Exoprimal in March 2027, and then turning the game's servers off in September.
  • The news comes from an "end of service announcement" published on the official Exoprimal website, where it is mentioned: "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.".
  • As of today, 25th November 2026, the game's four Survival Passes have already been taken off the PS Store.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Capcom has confirmed it'll be delisting its multiplayer dinosaur shooter Exoprimal in March 2027, and then turning the game's servers off in September.

The news comes from an "end of service announcement" published on the official Exoprimal website, where it is mentioned: "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.".

As of today, 25th November 2026, the game's four Survival Passes have already been taken off the PS Store.

Then, on 30th March 2027, Exoprimal and all its DLC and any other content will be removed from all storefronts.

Finally, the "end of service" phase and complete shutdown of Exoprimal is scheduled for 29th September 2027.

Industry observers note that "Exoprimal will no longer be playable after the end of service," Capcom confirms. While the game did receive a physical release on a disc, it requires an internet connection to servers in order to play. With those gone, Exoprimal will stop functioning no matter whether you own it physically or digitally.

Capcom has enjoyed an incredible PS5 generation with multiple critically-acclaimed releases, but Exoprimal is one of the few titles it put out that fell below the standards it set. That's not to say Exoprimal was bad, though — far from it.

In our own Exoprimal PS5 review, we awarded it a 7/10 and called it a "white-knuckle fusion of Overwatch and Gears of War". However, competition in the multiplayer space is strong, and it appears the game didn't do enough to sustain a big enough playerbase for Capcom to justify keeping the servers turned on.

Now, in less than a year, Exoprimal will be delisted and rendered completely unplayable.

The game is still full price on the PS Store, but between now and March 2027 (when the delisting occurs), I do imagine Capcom will hand it some steep discounts so those still curious can try it for cheap.

Did you play Exoprimal and enjoy it? Let us know in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever's absolutely had me enthralled, as per my review (and about 220+ hours of my actual life), but that's not to say there aren't issues. Over the weekend and going on into this week, Blizzard's had to play whack-a-mole with both exploits and what appears to be a long-standing bug affecting one of the tanking classes' core mechanics.

First, those exploits—players discovered that lockboxes contained a sort of quantum loot, in that the actual roll of the lockboxes seemed tied to the player peeking inside of them, rather than what was inside regardless. If you turned off auto-loot, you can open a lockbox without actually pulling the loot into your bag. Then, if you sent that lockbox to another player via mail, they'd get something different.

Recent findings suggest that essentially, players could simply play a game of mass pass-the-parcel to ensure favorable lockbox results, further busting up the economy after the Blackmaw Hold drama earlier this month. That's since been hotfixed, simply disabling the mechanic, with a more elegant solution to come further down the road: "Today, we’re working on a proper fix that restores the ability to peek and partially loot lockboxes, and makes them otherwise work as intended.".

Meanwhile, the Obsidian Sentinel in Uldaman was briefly rendered lootless. As spotted by WoWHead, players could hop into the dungeon and repeatedly rinse the boss to grab a cheeky 18 or so gold in 15 minutes by vendoring the loot as a max-level character.

While that's not really game-breaking (instance lockouts are limited to five per hour), if you had an organised group of level 60s all funnelling gold to the same guy—like, say, if you were a streamer with a dedicated fanbase that didn't mind wasting a quarter of an hour, or if you were a large-scale RMT operation—there's a bigger problem.

That lootless state turned out to be a band-aid, as Blizzard simply lowered the vendor costs later.

Perhaps the biggest hiccup over the past weekend, though, is the fact that Sunder Armor (and other armor-reducing effects like faerie fire) very well might just not do anything. I hopped in-game to test it on my warrior and saw no noticeable difference between Sunder Armor in both dungeons and the overworld while fighting lower level targets, though my testing capabilities were limited solo, since armor is affected by the level of whoever's attacking the target: And if I rock up to an on-level elite in a dungeon at 60, I tend to die before I can get a good sample.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Fortunately, I don't need to be too thorough. There's a lot more comprehensive math and log-testing on this github post: "Once an armor debuff goes on, players' and pets' hits barely move, same as the report states. About 5% of the armor drop actually indicates up in the damage, and more stacks don't help." The evidence is all pretty convincing.

According to recent reports, while those other exploits are annoying oopsies, arguably just a result of players—who find edge cases like water finds cracks—stress-testing the system? The Sunder Armor bug is sort of huge, since that's one of the protection warrior's main group utilities (aside from being a tanky meatshield). It still appears to be filling its primary role of threat generation, but: Yikes.

There's no mention of it in the hotfixes, but I'll update this article if one pops up in the coming days.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap.
  • Sources indicate that the hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website.
  • Sources indicate that "Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected consumers was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.

Sources indicate that the hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website. It's designed to address one issue, this being that "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background".

Sources indicate that "Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix. "This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Sometimes a change that is notable to many owners might end up sitting and waiting until we are able to release the driver. The fixes that make it in are based in part on your feedback in the Driver Feedback threads and partly on how realistic it is for us to rapidly address them. These fixes (and many more) will be incorporated into the next official driver release, at which time the hotfix driver will be taken down.

"To be sure, these Hotfix drivers are beta, optional and provided as-is. They are run through a much abbreviated QA process. The sole reason they exist is to get fixes out to you more rapidly. The safest option is to wait for the next WHQL certified driver. But we know that many of you are willing to try these out.".

Sources indicate that unfortunately, it seems that based on some testing by users on r/Nvidia, the hotfix makes the situation with excessive SSD writing less bad than it is with 621.24, but doesn't eliminate the problem entirely. According to one of these users, 621.35 stops the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reduces the amount that's being written when the matter's at its peak, but doesn't prevent some excessive writing creeping in if hardware is left running for extended periods or left idling overnight.

Given that, rolling back to 621.01 still appears to be the most effective way of keeping the writes at an acceptable level while waiting for Nvidia to release a fresh driver than can permanently do away with the problem. One would hope it won't take too long, especially given the 621.24 driver still doesn't look to have been pulled offline so no one else grabs it prior to a fix arriving.

It has been revealed that if you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's only writing a matter of MB or chunks of GB.

Recent findings suggest that so far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. The question is "by how much?".

In a recent development, reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that 1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild.

  • Recent findings suggest that in the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that 1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-fresh sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

It has been revealed that in much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise latest players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.

Recent findings suggest that in the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies. "They've gone into these levels in a sensible way to fix some practical problems with them, like some problems where you might be able to climb up to a place that you shouldn't have been able to climb up before," he commented.

It has been revealed that the Thief remaster team have taken more liberties, seemingly, with some of the Thief Gold maps. "Because some of the levels that were introduced in Thief Gold - they felt quite blocky and quite rushed, maybe, as you go through them," Grayshon explained. "But our team again, they've been able to go through and completely renovate some of these levels. The Opera House now feels in some parts like an actual Opera House, instead of a couple of blocky rooms. So I think players will really look at these and think, oh yeah, these kinds of details make sense, without it being too disruptive or too immersion breaking…".

According to recent reports, "One particular - maybe people will consider infamous - level of the Gold package would be the Thieves Guild," Grayshon added. "The Thieves Guild is, if I were to sum it up kind of briefly, it is maybe two hours of walking through what feels like sewers, the same environment over and over again. There was no real visual distinction as to where you are in the level.

"So, we acknowledged pretty rapidly that we need to go in and look at the Thieves Guild and fix it up, and what we've been able to do is texture it a lot more effectively. Give areas distinct looks, without compromising any of the gameplay again, like I mentioned. So we've put a bit more signposting around as well. Nothing that's going to be intrusive or immersion breaking again. Just kind of pointing the player in the right direction, as well as some other little things that I'm not going to spoil too much, but I think players will maybe appreciate the effort that we've done for this one.".

In general, Nightdive's broad aim has been "bringing those Gold levels up to the quality of the original and then taking all of those levels and then bumping them up to the next level - almost Thief 2 levels of quality in its environment design, especially in some of the mansions, and some of the later levels," Grayshon said. "That's the level we were aiming for.".

I have Several Thoughts about Grayshon's thoughts above (yes, people who dislike huffy armchair theory, this is your cue to skip to the comments). One is that I continue to dislike "immersion" as an ideal, though I recognise that many devs just use it as easy shorthand for a bunch of ways of doing art, sound and interface design. I think it often translates to uninvestigated enthusiasm for photorealistic fidelity and experiences that feel "smooth" and "engaging" enough to induce a kind of chemical trance. Many of the games I consider most valuable are cranky and unwilling and jarring, requiring you to think critically about the simulation rather than 'losing yourself' inside it. As regards the original Thief specifically, I enjoy how its nigh-magical stealth induces feelings of wavering dissociation, and keeps me guessing about the solidity of my own body.

In a recent development, secondly, there's the age-old argument that if you're going to preserve a game faithfully, you should preserve what it did badly. The Thieves Guild is a legend among players, much as Blighttown is among Dark Souls players and the Library is among fans of Halo: Combat Evolved. You learn much about the methodology of Thief at large from the guild's stifling contours, and it's thrilling to witness a bunch of very smart designers take a swing at a concept and not quite connect. I'll try to hold onto that rousing sentiment, when I'm playing the remaster and struggling to remember where they hid that damn vase.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a brief moment, Sauron ruled above all in The Rings of Power season 3, even likening his power to 'The One'. No, not the One Ring, but an even higher power – Eru Iluvatar, Middle-earth's answer to God.

While J.R.R. Tolkien largely kept The One away from the machinations of Middle-earth in his works (free will still exists in this fantasy world), Eru Iluvatar is a fascinating figure that bears further examination. The deity will also likely factor into The Rings of Power season 4, so it's time to get a headstart on who exactly He is.

Some spoilers for The Rings of Power season 3 ending follow.

Eru Iluvatar – also known as The One – is the creator of the world of Arda and its continents, including Middle-earth.

While he manifested the literal space of Middle-earth, The One left it up to angelic beings known as the Ainur and Valar (themselves created by Eru) to sculpt the land and create life within it.

Recent findings suggest that eru Iluvatar rarely intervenes in matters in the world below, with the leader of the Ainur, Manwe, designated to – in effect – be his eyes and ears. Tolkien wrote of the godlike figure: "He was appointed to be, in the fullness of time, the first of all Kings: lord of the realm of Arda and ruler of all that dwell therein.".

Digging deeper into Tolkien's works reveals that Eru Iluvatar was planning to take mortal form in Middle-earth's Seventh Age. With Middle-earth actually being our planet, Tolkien lined up the years so Eru could feasibly be Jesus Christ. That idea only surfaced in a handful of correspondence, however, and never made it into the full literature. Even then, it's only an in-universe belief held by some religious observers.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

As of The Rings of Power, Iluvatar is still worshipped as the one true God – especially in Numenor. Which makes Sauron's declaration that his power will make him stand above The One the worst possible sacrilege imaginable. So, will he descend from the heavens to ensure something is done? Well, about that….

Unless it deviates heavily from the source material, Eru Iluvatar will never show up – in a literal sense, anyway.

It has been revealed that spoilers for The Rings of Power season 4 follow, but with Sauron surrendering to Al-Pharazon, the Prime Video series is now on the path laid down by Tolkien, one which sees Numenor's ruler believing his power to be absolute. We won't go into specific details here, but Iluvatar does intervene at one point in one of Middle-earth's most shocking moments.

Eru's proxies and servants have also appeared in The Rings of Power. The Secret Fire, the power used by Iluvatar to create the world, appeared before Gandalf in season 3 and bestowed upon him the quest to unite once more with Pallando to help stop Sauron.

The Great Eagles have also turned up on multiple occasions, and they are emissaries of Iluvatar's right-hand angel Manwe and show up at moments of great importance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

In an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

The star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do.".

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

As you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

Sources indicate that on the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

Industry observers note that "Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that.".

Recent findings suggest that total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

The Witcher 4 is targeting a release in 2028, which will be 13 years after The Witcher 3 came out, as long as there aren't any delays. CD Projekt Red is working to the same timescale as Rockstar, and both developers even did the same thing of having a game in a different series release in the middle of it: Red Dead Redemption 2 for the latter and Cyberpunk 2077 for the former.

To that end, CD Projekt Red believes it can deliver a similar leap in quality.

"We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 — I think so, yes," stated joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski.

"It's been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better-looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game. So yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.".

In a recent development, just like Rockstar Games, marketing for The Witcher 4 will be backed by PlayStation, as CD Projekt Red has already signed a collaboration with Sony. GTA 6 has just been marketed as playing best on PS5, but that might not be true.

Instead, the Polish team will likely be more about main and side quest design, your abilities, and character customisation.

Recent findings suggest that on whether the release of GTA 6 and what CD Projekt Red has seen of it has impacted the development of its own games, Nowakowski responded: "We have certain ambitions when it comes to Witcher [4] and Cyberpunk 2; they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6. "The board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang, after which the board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candour and ability to lead Nvidia," the tech giant confirmed. "In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.".

It has been revealed that "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," added recently appointed chairman Harvey Jones, who'll remain in the post following Huang's return. Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO during Huang's short break, will go back to just being chief financial officer.

Sources indicate that "I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang declared. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.".

It has been revealed that oh, and Nvidia's board added that the independent investigation they set in motion "in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort" will "proceed to conclusion". Huang "fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it", they noted.

Since resigning amid the scandal, Huang had made it clear he'd be open to returning to his post if the Nvidia board okayed it and had several powerful people either call for his reinstatement or declare they'd consider hiring him. "The country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the organization, but the American economy," one such advocate, US president Donald Trump, has reportedly posted to cursed hellcape Truth social. Huang is a "great patriot and national treasure", the Trumpeter added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers for the end of Mass Effect 3 follow, naturally.

You know what? I didn't have many questions left at the end of Mass Effect 3. Joker was a robot now. His robot girlfriend was perhaps less of a robot? Shepard converted herself into a dotfile to make the Reapers chill out, and Buzz Aldrin's talents lie in areas other than voice acting.

Industry observers note that I had plenty of questions when BioWare announced Mass Effect 5 was gonna be a thing though. Could you really write a Mass Effect story in the radically changed galaxy we were left with at the end of Shepard's adventure? Apparently, you could. In a recent AMA on Reddit (via IGN), BioWare writer Cat Valente wrote that the now-cancelled Mass Effect sequel's team put a lot of work into handling ME3's endings "in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off, [or] at least not piss them off completely".

According to recent reports, the goal, says Valente, was to write a continuation of Mass Effect's narrative that "wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another". That tracks with what we've heard before: leaks have suggested ME5 was set to more or less wrap all the previous game's endings into one (Deus Ex: Invisible War style, hell yeah).

In a recent development, of course, it'd have to do that while allowing BioWare "to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream videogame and not a post-modern 3000 page novel", adds Valente. "Not for nothing, guys, but that's *kind of a tall fucking order*. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be *really hard*".

The sheer challenge of creating a coherent, satisfying follow-up to ME3 that took into account everyone's choices had Valente, at one point, "thinking *god, if I'd known when I finished ME3 that I'd be one of the people who had to find the mops and buckets to clean up that mess...*".

Sources indicate that nevertheless, she reckons the studio did eventually alight on a way of handling it that made sense. "Yes, there was an answer, yes, I know it, as least inasmuch as I know what it was when I was working there… We knew all the discourse on the endings, of course we did, and I do think as a fan I would have been happy with the solution (at least what it was when I left) if I booted up the game having had nothing to do with it".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

According to recent reports, "Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it.".

Downing Street went on to address the glitch of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

Sources indicate that the leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else.".

GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

According to recent reports, this state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

These agreements cover the presence of CDPR games on subscription services such as PlayStation Plus, but also "our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign" - which is the bit we're particularly interested in.

Here's a bit of the transcription via our friends at VGC:.

"Just today, we signed fresh partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign.".

"This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years.".

Sources indicate that A lot of people are now speculating that The Witcher 4's "collaboration" with Sony may be akin to what Take-Two has done with GTA 6, pushing the whole "plays best on PS5" campaign and restricting how Xbox is allowed to advertise the game. For example, GTA's launch trailer was solely focused around PS5 for an exclusive window.

It's key to highlight that this is just speculation though, and there may be aspects of these agreements that aren't exclusive at all. We've seen CDPR titles like Cyberpunk 2077 on Xbox Game Pass in the not too distant past, for example, so the PlayStation Plus agreement doesn't necessarily mean Game Pass is out the window.

It has been revealed that let's wait and see what happens with this, but just keep in mind that we could be looking at a situation where The Witcher 4 gets a bigger push on PlayStation than Xbox when it (hopefully) releases in 2028. We'll also leave you with a fun GTA comparison quote from joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski about the difference between Witcher 3 and 4!

"I’m not going to make a deep dive, full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6, but of course, we did look at the game, we did see the differences... we believe there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4. It’s been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better-looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in the last couple of years, when Walt Disney Animation has released a movie during its long-coveted Thanksgiving slot, it's been a sequel that became a $1 billion hit. However, it's been a long while since the House of Mouse released an original title that really cast a magical spell on audiences. I was hopeful about the next upcoming Disney movie, Hexed, especially after seeing the first reactions. But now that the reviews are here, I'm afraid we might have to wait longer for another real Disney winner.

It's never especially a great sign when a studio lifts its review embargo the day before a movie is set to release. As the reviews roll in this morning, there are a lot of complaints about it. Let's start with the thoughts of Roger Ebert's Peter Sobczynski:.

On the one hand, it’s bright and colorful, with enough goofiness and action to serve as an acceptable diversion for family audiences over the long holiday weekend. But it’s hobbled by an overly familiar story that never really does anything to make it memorable.

Hexed is the first non-sequel to come out from Walt Disney Animation since 2023's Wish, which earned a 48 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from critics and made just $254 million worldwide. It's too early to call this movie's true RT score, but there's similarly middling reception so far. AV Club's Jacob Oller had this to say:.

Recent findings suggest that the basic beats of the ensuing adventure are painfully predictable, with all the rescue attempts, training sequences, familial bonding moments, and climactic showdowns coming right on cue. But these checkboxes aren’t just predictable, they’re the most obvious versions of themselves.

The movie features Hailee Steinfeld voicing a rebellious teenage witch named Billie, as she finds out she has magical powers. Rashida Jones voices her overprotective mom, and Jodie Foster voices the movie's villainous witch, Celeste. The movie was co-written by Walt Disney Animation's CCO Jared Bush and Moana 2's Dana Ledoux Miller.

Both of these reviews seem to sing a similar tune. They seem to find Hexed to be predictable and pretty unimaginative. The Guardian's Benjamin Lee had comparable thoughts, writing these words to go with his two-out-of-five-star review:.

According to recent reports, like Wish, it’s a film clearly crafted by people who have deep affection for the Disney back catalogue but who can’t quite turn reverence for what came before into any real idea of where to take things going forward. Again, there’s something too calculated and businesslike, with nods to previous films and regurgitated life lessons, and while Disney adventures have always emerged from a Goliath-sized mega-corporation, the best ones can make you briefly forget that.

Sources indicate that then there's Variety's Guy Lodge, who pointed out how Hexed is perhaps particularly disappointing in the wake of the stop-motion movie Wildwood, which came out last month. Here are some of his thoughts:.

Sources indicate that the Hollywood Reporter's Angie Han had more positive things to say about Hexed, but made a point of saying the visuals dazzled her more than the storyline itself. In her words:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

More than as a fairy tale, an inspirational fable or a complex exploration of the bonds between mothers and daughters, Hexed shines brightest as a travelogue through an enchanting world only accessible through the portal of a screen. If that’s not enough to make for a fresh cinematic classic, it’s more than enough to make for a pleasurably transportive trip to the theater.

According to recent reports, it's certainly worth pointing out that Hexed will likely be much more of a hit with its target audience of young girls. That remains to be seen, but not all the reviews are bummers. The Wrap's Amelia Emberwing celebrated the movie's girl power and made these comments:.

This is a film that is boldly sure of its own identity, and refuses to be anything other than blissfully witchy and womanly. The girl power aspects never extend into girl-bossery, and the film offers not just exciting normals that should be discussed more often in young adult media, but an ending that, while the logical conclusion of the story, also goes against traditional Disney norms and the standard teen movie tropes.

According to recent reports, with regard to the box office, Hexed is projected to make around $40 million behind the new Hunger Games, which isn't great. As a lifelong Disney fan who wants to support original animation and see it thrive, I'm concerned. The studio really needed an original hit, and so far the news isn't trending up.

According to recent reports, as with all reviews we talk about, we definitely recommend you check out the movie anyway, especially if you were already looking forward to it. Who knows, maybe you'll disagree? Oh, and Hexed has a Lilo & Stitch short before the movie not to miss. Hexed hits theaters on Wednesday!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

2027 will likely be a pivotal year for Cyberpunk 2 as it rockets towards full production, with CD Projekt Red anticipating significant expansion to the sequel's development team.

Since the summer, the number of people working on Cyberpunk 2 has increased from 184 to 199, which doesn't seem like much, but this is a steady process.

By the end of next year, management expects there to be a total of around 320 devs — a team size that would be comparable to the 500-strong studio that's at the moment preparing The Witcher 4 for its 2028 release.

In other words, we can probably assume Cyberpunk 2 will leave early production in the relatively near future — and that's a substantial deal, because it means that the bones of the project are basically locked in place.

CDPR's Karolina Gnaś, who maintains relationships with the company's investors, reiterates that "good progress" is being made with Cyberpunk 2 — with further comments suggesting that there have been no internal delays.

The thing is, we're probably not going to see the Cyberpunk 2077 successor until The Witcher 4 is out, which seems a rather daunting prospect.

Sources indicate that but it's worth remembering that CDPR is now essentially split between two major studios — one in Poland (The Witcher 4) and one in the US (Cyberpunk 2). The organization's grown massively since The Witcher 3 first released over a decade ago.

What are your hopes and dreams for Cyberpunk 2? Let those expectations run wild in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fuse Games, the developer of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has said it "didn't dream" the pod racing game's background character Biddy Blas would become as popular as he has.

In a recent development, since Galactic Racer's release in October, Blas - who resembles a short, humanoid crocodile (officially a crocin) - has become a viral sensation. The combination of his unexpected swagger and ridiculous high-pitched Huttese monologues - performed irresistibly by actor Richard Summers-Calvert - have made him a fan favourite, especially his catchphrase "scrib doon" (which means "write it down").

Industry observers note that "Here's a name for you, amateur!" Blas tells the player upon meeting them, albeit in Huttese. "Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!".

In a recent development, fuse Games shared a comment from Biddy Blas creator and Galactic Racer narrative designer Ren Alex-Rose about the character's success. "We always suspected Biddy Blas would be a popular member of the Galactic League, but we didn't dream of just how popular he'd become," Alex-Rose remarked.

"He was an incredibly enjoyable character to build, from our early ideation of a small, angry non-human character (who we lovingly referred to as our cast's 'chaos goblin') to recording his sometimes-absurdist dialogue with Blas' voice actor, who took the crocin to a whole fresh level.

In a recent development, "It's been great watching Biddy Blas emerge into his assured self, as well as seeing the community embrace him for it. He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly.".

It has been revealed that blas' breakout success was praised by Lucasfilm producer Craig Derrick, who mentioned his social feeds were filled with posts about Galactic Racer, though mostly about Biddy Blas. And the enthusiasm actor Richard Summers-Calvert was greeted with during October's MCM Comic-Con in London, which I attended, was palpable. There's a nice video of him doing Blas' voice on Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that star Wars: Galactic Racer was awarded a full five stars in Eurogamer's review. "Both a surprisingly fun Roguelite campaign and a racing treat for Criterion fans, this is just wonderful stuff," wrote Christian Donlan.

Here is an overview of the game, via CI Games:.

Lords of the Fallen II is a dark fantasy action RPG where brutal, Soulslike combat meets a world splitting at its core. Battle against the darkness in an epic adventure across a shattered kingdom. One world. Two realms. No mercy.

In a recent development, realm by realm, nation after nation, the Umbral darkness consumed all in Her path. Now, centuries later, only one Kingdom remains; a sacred land, shrouded by an ancient force. Or so it was….

Stolen by the Gods themselves, mankind is left forsaken, defenseless against the darkness. Unless this force is restored, the shadow of death will devour all. But how do you kill… an immortal?

A hero must rise, for a God to fall.

  • Recent findings suggest that these are all the fences that are available in GTA 6.
  • Let's take a look now at these options in more details.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there are seven different GTA 6 fences you can find, with locations all over the map. But which you’ll have access to depends on where you are in Jason and Lucia’s journey as you work though all the GTA 6 Missions. They all offer different rates for different goods, with two that are specific to cars, so it’s handy to keep track of what your options are and where you can find them.

Recent findings suggest that these are all the fences that are available in GTA 6. However, they’re not all available at the same time and all offer different services:.

Let's take a look now at these options in more details.

According to recent reports, brian is Jason’s earliest contact in the criminal world, so it’s not surprising that he would be your first fence. But it’s a good thing that he becomes inaccessible after the end of Chapter 1, because his rates are as low as they go.

Industry observers note that another early game fence, leaving narcotics at Donnie’s trailer will get you a slightly better rate than going through Brian, while it’s the same rate for jewelry and marked bills. But Donnie becomes inaccessible even earlier than Brian, so if you have drugs to sell, make sure you drop them off in good time before the Swamped mission.

In Chapter 2, you’ll unlock the ability to fence stolen cars when you meet Moses. He also has a list he’s willing to pay more for. He won’t take anything with a tracker, though – you’ll have to wait until Chapter 3 before you’re able to sell these more advanced cars.

It has been revealed that dunk becomes an available fence after the aptly named Slam Dunk mission in Chapter 2. When that mission is complete, you’ll be able to find Dunk’s trailer near the centre of Port Gellhorn. He doesn’t pay very much, but he stays available as you progress through the game, so if you find yourself on the western side of the map and don’t want to bother driving over to Vice City, he’s still a viable option.

Industry observers note that once you make it to the massive city in Chapter 3, you’ll be offered a mission called Tyrone, which will introduce you to one of the fences who will be useful for the rest of the game. Tyrone pays highly for narcotics, and also at a medium rate for jewelry and marked bills. Note that you might be better off going to Yasmani for those other two though – he’s not far away, as you can see below.

Sources indicate that found not too far away from Tyrone, and unlocked not too long afterwards, is Yasmani. He pays highly for jewelry and marked bills, so it’s best to split those off to him while taking any narcotics you’ve picked up over to Tyrone.

Finally in Chapter 3, you’ll unlock Randy, who can deal with all kinds of cars regardless of their trackers. Like Moses, he also has a list of desired vehicles, which can be turned into him for high payouts – but he’ll take anything you happen to lift, too.

According to recent reports, one of the best things to emerge from Grand Theft Auto over the years has been the community's truly spectacular stunts: players soaring under bridges, leaping across buildings, and more. And with GTA 6's release this week, we've seen the first signs of the trend continuing in a brand-newly introduced world.

Recent findings suggest that this TikTok video by user Gstitz from early in GTA 6, for instance, claims to be the "world's first" demonstration of a Mallard flying sideways between a narrow gap in a large building. It takes several attempts, but they eventually pull off the stunt without crashing or broken parts.

Recent findings suggest that another video from Hazardous is a more grounded (literally) look at Grand Theft Auto 6, and shows the YouTuber flinging motorbikes and cars around the map as they explore promising high-risk jumps. Some of these locations are tied to in-game challenges, so there are certainly breadcrumbs placed by Rockstar to encourage such ventures.

Granted, these are far from the truly absurd stunts we've seen in prior Grand Theft Auto games. But as a firing gun for the wider community, it's a great start. They're also among the most impressive things we've seen in GTA 6's opening week.

It's doubtless been an eventful few days though. Players have been entranced by the slapstick violence and in-game social media. Even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has praised the game, despite not having time to actually play it. Eurogamer editor-in-chief Chris Tapsell also came away impressed, lauding it in his five star GTA 6 review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that as a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's crucial questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.

In a recent development, in this first-person co-op platformer - created in Unreal Engine, with both online multiplayer and splitscreen support - you and a mate play Luna and Foam, two rock-hopping magic children with nothing better to do than lob hermetically sealed felines through tears in reality itself. Egad! Apparently the cats are fine with this. You'll have to work together to traverse astral watercolour landscapes, hurling and catching the kitty while trying not to tumble into the abyss.

You can also catch each other's arms and haul each other onto safe ground, which puts this in approximately the same bracket as the well-liked Peak. Other Neat Tricks include bouncing the starry-eyed moggies from soap bubbles, swinging from strands of green snot (?), and springboarding from tornadoes.

In a recent development, the cats remain blissfully unconscious throughout, smiling in their slumber right up to the point when you crack their crystal prisons. If you're familiar with cats, the penalty for breaking their domes may seem rather mild. I was hoping for something along the lines of Peter Puppy having a rage-out in Earthworm Jim.

Would it surprise you to learn that one or more of the people working on Whisk is a former developer of Sky: Children of Light, the open world swoop 'em up from thatgamecompany? I imagine you might not consider that startling – the two games both look a little like the result of somebody inhaling burnt banana skins. But you might be giddier to hear that one or more of the Whisk devs is also a veteran of Riot's Counter-Strike descendant Valorant. I'm pretty sure Valorant doesn't have any cat-throwing, but I'm prepared to be proven wrong.

According to recent reports, it's coming to Steam early access early in 2027, and there's a demo on Steam right now with eight levels and 10 cats to "rescue". People are already bragging in the forums about their leaderboard placements – monsters!

According to recent reports, anyway, Arizona Sunshine was a significant deal 10 years ago, so it'll be fascinating to see how well it fares on modern non-VR platforms. The game is already available to pre-order on the Xbox Store at a low price of £21.99 / $24.99, and it also seemingly comes with Xbox Play Anywhere support (meaning you get a free PC copy too).

We'll leave you with more details on Arizona Sunshine below, launching for Xbox on January 21st of 2027.

Recent findings suggest that sharpen your machete and grab your friends. Arizona Sunshine® brings its award-winning zombie apocalypse to explosive third-person action, featuring online and split-screen co-op, brutal combat, dark humor, and Buddy, your loyal zombie-chomping canine companion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

"… We will continue to take community feedback into account as we carefully evaluate the possibility of permanently enabling travel between the North American and European data centers, as well as opening travel between other physical data centers," via the Lodestone.

This is a big deal and I'm very excited.

I play Final Fantasy 14 on the US servers—which is a problem, because I live in the UK. I do so because, well, some of my closest friends are on those servers, too; but also because there's a slightly livelier roleplay community bustling on the US side of things, and I'm a roleplayer who likes squeezing my warrior of light like he's a stress toy.

It has been revealed that as a result, I've often stared longingly at the people who play in the UK due to the crime of my time zone: Unable to play with my UK friends, unable to join a static raiding group that starts at a reasonable hour, and unable to play the game without terrible animation lock on my abilities. Unless I, say, broke ToS and used an addon that brought me on-par with people who have 30 ping, hypothetically. Which I don't do.

Square Enix has thrown open these doors, however, to mainly deal with congestion troubles:.

"As peak play times differ between North America and Europe, another physical data center may be less crowded and serve as a viable option when login queues on your usual data center are long. While players connecting from geographically distant locations may experience increased latency, we encourage you to try playing on a different physical data center before the expansion launches.".

However, they know that people like me have expressed their yearning to hop between the good ol' USA and Europe: "However, we have received ongoing feedback from players wishing to travel between the North American and European data centers, and many players in both regions are able to communicate in English even when it is not their first language.".

All in all, this'll be a huge quality of life improvement. There might be some difficulties, though: raiding culture can vary drastically even between logical datacenters like Aether and Crystal, let alone between continents. However, I'd be shocked if the differences between US and EU raiding cultures were insurmountable; JP and US? Might be a bigger deal.

Chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation. They are right now being investigated on suspicion of selling infringing reproductions.

Reported by Gamespark, the police cracked down on the operation which involved the seizure of around $300,000 of goods related to the figurines.

The investigation started in May, after police received reports from concerned members of the public about the Tifa figurines. They were made from different materials than official figurines, and after confirming the illegitimacy of these products with the rights holders, Square Enix, police determined these businesses were not authorised to be producing such goods and went to work.

Industry observers note that the appearance of these counterfeits were deemed identical to the real merch, and therefore the alleged crime was deemed infringement of official goods. These counterfeits also came in different sizes, some of which were more expensive than the originals and customisabile.

Looking at pictures taken by local outlet Shangguan News (and put side-by-side by Automaton), you can see the official Tifa figurine (right) next to the counterfeit version (left). Both show Tifa in a blue dress, though the materials used are clearly different.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Skate, the free-to-play skateboarding game that's still in Early Access, is ditching its seasonal approach moving forward, publisher EA has confirmed.

The always-online, shared world game has been getting fairly regular updates since its launch back in September 2025, and it's all been modelled around Seasons. Following the next update — 0.33, launching 1st December — this system will be dropped.

No more Seasons also means no more Skate Passes or Tix; instead, the development team is prioritising "regular, agile content updates", saying it'll be able to launch features earlier and get active feedback from players:.

"Moving away from rigid season blocks gives the development team the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle. This means we can deploy work-in-progress mechanics and gather your direct feedback to continuously shape and build upon San Vansterdam. We’ve started this with in-game testing of features such as Spot Battles, Block Parties, and Prox Chat before rolling it out officially, and we’re going to continue with this process to ensure we get YOUR feedback on what works/what doesn’t.".

On top of this incoming change, the game's next patch is a fairly hefty one:.

Sources indicate that the competitive game mode S.K.A.T.E. is being added, with various spots on the map where you can play, or you can use the Throwdown menu to create your own challenges.

Another major feature in this enhancement is (optional) proximity chat, which will be available on all maps in the game.

For those that don't know, proximity chat is a version of voice chat that means you can only hear players that are close by.

Version 0.33 is also adding and updating locations in San Vansterdam, such as the RINQ Hotel, the Loading Bay of The Vault, and Pump House Park on the Isle of Grom.

On top of that, the upgrade introduces upcoming cosmetics, music, and more.

Industry observers note that it seems there's a good amount to check out in the upcoming update. It'll be interesting to see how the game evolves now that it's discontinuing Seasons.

  • Sources indicate that kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A hacker who pleaded guilty to the 2022 hacking breach of Rockstar Games, which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net, has been released under supervision. The hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has also a five year long serious crime prevention order which will restrict what he can do online.

The BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence. On licence means his release is subject to a number of conditions. According to the UK Government website, the exact nature of these conditions varies from person to person and case to case, as they've got be "considered necessary and proportionate". However, things like needing not to commit any more crimes, not travel abroad, and live under the supervision of community offender manager are cited as part of a set of "standard licence conditions" outlined by the government site.

Sources indicate that kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online. It includes bans from using both Telegram and Discord.

According to the BBC, the judge told Kurtaj Yyou are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again." City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

Kurtaj pleaded guilty on November 16th at Woolwich Crown Court to the 2022 Rockstar Games hack, as well as a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Now aged 21, he was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely, due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial.

In a recent development, 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by the 2022 hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the firm contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by 'Cyberleek' posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent organization Take-Two rapidly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

According to recent reports, cyberleek has since claimed to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 onto the net, while withholding a main executable file they threatened to release subsequently. Online sources claim the executable has now also been leaked, though this has not been independently verified.
